view_title: Column grid master for บ้านครอบครัวไทยเป็นสุข 5 (2-storey RC house). Four printed x-lines 1..4 at 3.50/2.20/3.00 m (8.70 m overall) and six printed y-lines ง'/ง/ค'/ค/ข/ก over 11.40 m overall. Taken from S-01 (หน้า19, แปลนฐานราก+แปลนชั้นล่าง 1:100), cross-checked against S-01/1 (หน้า20, แปลนฐานรากแผ่) and S-02 (หน้า21, แปลนชั้นบน). Origin = ง × 1, the topmost/leftmost *named* line; the two printed prime lines ง' and ค' therefore sit at negative / intermediate positions.

warnings: PRINTED PRIME LINES BREAK §4's PRIME-ORDERING RULE, AND THE PRINTED LABEL WINS. This sheet set prints two of its own primed grid bubbles, ง' (-2.80) and ค' (3.20), drawn identically to the plain ง/ค/ข/ก bubbles. §4 says a prime is appended to the main grid ABOVE the line, and §4's ordering rule says the first line found scanning top-to-bottom takes one prime; the sheet obeys neither (ค' sits 0.80 ABOVE ค, so §4 would have called it ง'). §0.3 and §4's own exception forbid renaming a label the drawing supplies, so both are recorded verbatim as type 'named'. THE RULE THIS FILE USES INSTEAD, applied consistently: every dummy this extraction ADDS is named after the plain letter of its group and given the next prime count not already taken by a printed bubble, assigned in top-to-bottom order among the ADDED lines only. That gives ง'' (-3.80) → ง''' (-0.80) → ง'''' (2.00), which IS monotonic top-to-bottom among the added lines; only the printed ง' interleaves at -2.80. Prime COUNT therefore means 'how many primes were already taken', not absolute position. Do not 'fix' this by renumbering; the printed bubbles are the ground truth.

ORIGIN. y = 0.00 is ง, the topmost line whose bubble carries no prime, following the houses 01-05 convention (highest letter at the top of the sheet = origin) and §4's rule that a dummy may never take the origin. The two lines above it therefore carry negative pos_m: ง' -2.80 (printed) and ง'' -3.80 (added). x = 0.00 is grid 1, with 1' at -0.80.

DIMENSION CONVENTION IS MIXED ON THIS SET, AND IT MATTERS. The grid-bubble-to-grid-bubble dimensions (3.50 / 2.20 / 3.00 on x; 2.00 / 0.80 / 4.00 / 3.00 / 1.60 on y) are centreline dimensions and close exactly against the printed overall 8.70 and 11.40. Every LOCAL feature dimension on the same sheets (0.80, 0.65, 0.60, 0.30, 1.10, 3.90) scales to a member FACE, not a centreline - repeatedly about 0.10 m, i.e. half a 0.20 m beam, away from the line it appears to dimension. Every dummy line derived from a local dimension is flagged individually above. Where the two readings disagreed, the printed number was kept and the discrepancy recorded, per §4's rule against guessing a pos_m.

BOTH DIMENSION CHAINS CLOSE. x: 3.50 + 2.20 + 3.00 = 8.70, matching the printed overall on all three structural sheets. y: 2.00 + 0.80 + 4.00 + 3.00 + 1.60 = 11.40, matching the printed overall. The 0.80 printed beside ค'/ค is an auxiliary offset dimension drawn on its own short witness line, NOT a member of the main chain - adding it would give 12.20 and was the first wrong reading taken on this house.

NO DRAWING BREAK LINES ANYWHERE IN THIS SET. Checked explicitly at high magnification on S-01, S-01/1 and S-02 per the house-06 lesson: the building is 8.70 x 11.40 m, fits on the paper at 1:100 uninterrupted, and no double line with a zigzag symbol appears on any structural sheet. The x axis really is 4 lines and the y axis really is 6 printed lines.

THE CARPORT SLAB EAST OF GRID 4 GETS NO DUMMY GRID. The GS slab drawn 1.80 m beyond grid 4 on S-01 (แปลนชั้นล่าง) is bounded by a thin slab edge with no beam mark and no column at its corners, so per §4's explicit slab-edge exception it is a slab-only edge, not a structural line. Same for the 0.30-wide (S) strip just west of grid 2 between ง' and ง''', and the terrace edge 0.30 east of grid 2 below ข.
SINGLE BUILDING. Unlike บ้าน_ใหญ่_1ชั้น_01 this set covers one building only; §11a does not apply and there is no second grid master.
